Criteria:
- P1: Dependencies: does every step come after the steps whose results it needs? If a requirement of step B uses something that a requirement of step A creates (a name, a command, a connection, data, a schema, a part that is reused), B needs A. Name each missing dependency as 'A -> B' (A must finish before B) and say what B needs from A.
- P2: Coverage: is each requirement's work done by build and test steps that really do it?
- P3: Acceptance criteria: are they concrete and checkable?
- P4: Granularity: no duplicated steps and no step split into trivial pieces?

The research, verify, design and review steps and the order research -> design -> build -> test -> documents -> review come from a template and are correct. Steps listed as 'after: X' already depend on X (directly); a dependency through other steps also counts.

Material:
Requirements:
R1 [must] Write at least five unit tests for the function parse_date in dates.py.
R2 [must] Each test must check exactly one behaviour and have a descriptive name.
R3 [must] Add a test that checks parse_date raises ValueError for the input 31/02/2024.
R4 [must] Use pytest.mark.parametrize for the tests of valid dates.
R5 [must] Measure statement coverage and reach at least 80 % for dates.py.
R6 [could] You may also add property-based tests with Hypothesis for extra credit.
R7 [must] All tests must run with the single command pytest -q.

Plan steps:
research [research] Research the approach (requirements: -; after: -) criteria: every research question has an answer with sources; the answers name the options considered
verify [research] Check the research findings (requirements: -; after: research) criteria: every claim the design uses is supported by a source; unsupported claims are marked
design [design] Design the solution (requirements: -; after: verify) criteria: each part has a module and an interface; the skeleton runs; the design follows the constraints; C1 respected: Install pytest version 8 or newer in the virtual environment.
T1 [implement] Create parametrized unit tests for valid dates (requirements: R1, R2, R4, R7; after: design) criteria: At least five unit tests are present for parse_date; Each test checks exactly one behaviour and has a descriptive name; Tests for valid dates use pytest.mark.parametrize; All tests run with the command pytest -q
T2 [implement] Add test for invalid date exception (requirements: R3, R7; after: design) criteria: A test checks that parse_date raises ValueError for 31/02/2024; The test runs with pytest -q
T3 [implement] Configure coverage measurement for dates module (requirements: R5; after: design) criteria: Statement coverage for dates.py is measured; Coverage report can be generated with a single command
T4 [test] Verify coverage meets 80 percent threshold (requirements: R5; after: T3) criteria: Coverage report shows ≥ 80% statement coverage for dates.py
T5 [test] Add optional property‑based tests with Hypothesis (requirements: R6; after: T1, T2, T3) criteria: Property‑based tests are present and pass; Tests are included in the pytest run
T6 [document] Prepare coverage report screenshot (requirements: -; after: T4, T5) criteria: D2 exists: coverage report screenshot; it matches the finished, tested work
review [review] Final review (requirements: -; after: T6) criteria: every must requirement is met; every deliverable is present; C1 respected: Install pytest version 8 or newer in the virtual environment.; C2 respected: Do not change the code in dates.py; only add tests.
